gbm_population_evidence.quote: Methimazole in Patients With Progressive Glioblastoma

Subjects must have histologically or cytologically confirmed WHO grade 4 glioma (including tumors with molecularly defined grade 4 astrocytoma) for which a clinically indicated tumor resection is planned.

candidate_evidence.quote: it is hypothesized that reduced thyroid hormone production via oral methimazole intake will bolster the effectiveness of frontline therapy and extend survival by boosting H2S production and function within the tumor-bearing brain.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Participants with recurrent glioblastoma for whom surgical resection is indicated will have baseline peripheral blood pharmacodynamic assays (PBPD)

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: If they achieve a 10% increase in peripheral blood H2S concentrations, an additional 13 participants will receive this dose
Pharmacodynamic assays are intended to investigate drug and downstream drug-induced effects.

role_evidence.quote: The investigational drug, Methimazole is not FDA approved for brain tumors, but it is used to treat thyroid illnesses.

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: suppression of thyroid hormone signaling to augment endogenous H2S synthesis and signaling (transsulfuration)
arms: Surgical Resection, Pharmacodynamic Assays, and Methimazole

coder_notes: Active moiety given as INN thiamazole (registered as methimazole). Eligibility is 'WHO grade 4 glioma' without an IDH requirement, read as historical glioblastoma (D27C) together with title/conditions naming glioblastoma; possible inclusion of IDH-mutant grade 4 astrocytoma is not excluded. Regimen coded combination because the experimental arm adds physician's-choice secondary chemotherapy after the first 4-week methimazole cycle (unnamed, not a registered intervention, so not listed as an agent); first cycle is methimazole alone. Pharmacodynamic markers are peripheral blood H2S and thyroid hormone levels (not tumour molecular biomarkers), so no biomarker rows.
